cohort: The study included 15 women who experienced postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony during cesarean section and required uterine compression sutures after conservative medical and uterine massage treatment failed.
finding: All 15 cases treated with the new uterine compression suture technique were managed successfully, with no patients requiring hysterectomy or reoperation due to bleeding.
mod_finding: The new uterine compression suture technique was applied to women experiencing uterine atony during cesarean section.
